fixedIn: unknown (not established in the sources fetched)
behaviour: Crafting one snow block costs four snowballs while breaking it always yields six, allowing a repeatable net gain of two snowballs per cycle.

evidence.quote:
Now require only 4 snowballs to be crafted instead of 9.
** They still always drop 6 snowballs, allowing for an infinite source of snowballs.

implementationNote: Version-gate the snow-block recipe yield and block loot table; do not globally change the modern recipe. The record only confirms the behavior in Alpha 1.0.6; unknown boundary is not a refusal rule.

fixedIn: Alpha v1.0.17 (the next researched build with slimes restored)
behaviour: A miscalculation in the revised slime population limit caused natural slime spawning to be disabled in Alpha 1.0.14; slimes return by Alpha 1.0.17.

evidence.quote: A miscalculation in the new limit has now caused slimes to spawn only in strange locations, so natural slime spawning has now been disabled.
Slime spawning is BACK, because 1.0.14 disabled it as a bug and the research says not to infer a permanent removal.

implementationNote: Gate natural slime spawn eligibility off for exactly the affected profile; do not suppress slimes in neighboring Alpha builds. The existing HistoricalSpawnRules reportedly already applies this profile-specific absence.

fixedIn: Beta 1.6 (portal-ride crash listed among that release's fixes; exact patch boundary not narrowed further)
behaviour: Entering a Nether portal while riding a boat, minecart, or pig could crash the game and delete player data. Preserve this only as a documented danger, not by intentionally risking player saves.

evidence.quote: Entering a [[Nether portal]] while riding a [[boat]], [[minecart]], or [[pig]] will crash the game and delete the player data.
Fixed a game crash when riding a vehicle or animal into the Nether.

implementationNote: A safe compatibility simulation could dismount/deny the portal transition with a warning or isolated test fixture; never reproduce save deletion. Fixed patch within intervening Beta 1.2.x–1.6.x releases was not established, so unknown is deliberate.

fixedIn: Beta 1.3 first reupload (17:33 UTC, same release day)
behaviour: The original 17:13 client spawned a new or respawning player with 64 torches, a diamond pickaxe, shovel, axe, and 64 beds; the 17:33 reupload removed this debug code. Because the repo's build id does not distinguish the same-day artifacts, this must not be treated as applying to every Beta 1.3 client.

evidence.quote:
Beta 1.3 was uploaded at 17:13 UTC, this version contained debug code that spawns the player with 64 [[torch]]es, a [[diamond pickaxe]], a [[diamond shovel]], a [[diamond axe]], and 64 [[bed]]s upon respawning or creating a world.
Beta 1.3 was reuploaded at 17:33 UTC to remove the debug code

implementationNote: Only model this behind an explicit artifact sub-profile if the project can represent it; otherwise leave it unimplemented rather than applying to all beta_1_3 worlds.

behaviour: Before Beta 1.4, zombies and spiders only damaged the player when one block above the player's location; Beta 1.4 fixed attacks to hurt in all instances. The introduction build was not identified, so this is not a safe refusal boundary.

evidence.quote: Before this version, zombies and spiders only hurt the [[player]] if they were 1 block above their location.

implementationNote: Would require an entity attack hit/damage gate conditioned on historical profile and exact relative Y; introduction range remains unknown, so do not ship based only on these candidate ids.

behaviour: Trying to piston-push a block that is destroyed by piston movement could create invalid block 36 ('air') and crash rendering; related piston/redstone interactions could crash or soft-lock a world.

evidence.quote: Attempting to push a block that is destroyed by a [[piston]] will create block 36 air, which crashes the game when rendered. Upgrading a world rendered unplayable by this bug to [[Beta 1.7_01]] or later allows it to be played again.
Some blocks crash the game when attempted to be pushed or pulled. This also softlocks the world.

implementationNote: Can emulate only as a controlled block-movement failure or warning in the Beta 1.7 profile; do not corrupt modern chunk storage or crash the host JVM. Exclude from Beta 1.7_01 onward.

behaviour: Jumping erroneously awards a random 1–100 experience points; holding the jump key no longer auto-repeats. Prerelease 2 removes the XP debug code and restores continuous jumping. This is a single-build bug in the declared matrix, not a blanket rule for all prereleases before Pre2.

evidence.quote:
When the [[player]] jumps, their [[experience]] increases by a number between 1 and 100 experience.
* Continuous jumping by holding down the jump key is no longer possible.

Removed debug code causing jumping to increase experience.
* Continuous jumping by holding down the jump key is now possible again.

implementationNote: Server-side jump-event hook can grant the era's erroneous amount; client input handling must disable held-jump repeat only for this profile. Do not gate this as 'pre-Pre2' because Alpha/Beta builds before XP have no experience system.

behaviour: Snowfall temporarily destroys redstone dust, torches, saplings, and rails during the Pre1–Pre4 range; Pre5 fixes the regression. Keep the gate bounded to these four builds, not all versions earlier than Pre5.

evidence.ref: Beta 1.9 Prerelease 1 and Pre5 version evidence strings
evidence.quote: snowfall temporarily destroys redstone, torches, saplings and rails, a regression Pre5 fixes.

implementationNote: Weather/block-tick hook can remove only those affected block classes on snowfall ticks for the four listed profiles. Preserve neighboring pre-Pre1 and Pre5+ content.

behaviour: An explosion can destroy an End portal frame and drop it as an item in Pre3; Pre4 prevents the End portal from being broken by explosions. Single-build boundary: do not apply this to Pre2 or Pre4+.

evidence.ref: History > Java Edition > Beta 1.9 Prerelease 3 and Prerelease 4
evidence.quote: It can drop as an item due to explosions.
The End portal can no longer be broken by explosions.

implementationNote: Use a server-side explosion block-interaction hook to permit frame destruction/drop only for beta_1_9_pre_3; retain modern block entity/registry and portal logic otherwise.

behaviour: End portal frames emit light level 15 in Pre3; the value changes to level 1 in Pre4. This is a one-build visual/lighting state, not a range extending from Pre3 onward.

evidence.ref: History > Java Edition > Beta 1.9 Prerelease 3 / Prerelease 4
evidence.quote: Gives off a light level of 15.
Now emits light level of 1

implementationNote: Version-aware block luminance requires a narrow light-emission override for End Portal Frame states; verify propagation and lighting cache updates. Gate exactly Pre3.

behaviour: Silk Touch causes monster spawners to drop themselves in Pre4; Pre5 removes that drop. This is an exact-build drop rule and must not be generalized to all old versions.

evidence.ref: History > Java Edition > Beta 1.9 Prerelease 4 and 5
evidence.quote: Monster spawners now [[drop]] when mined using a [[tool]] enchanted with the new [[Silk Touch]] enchantment.
Monster spawners no longer drop when broken using a tool enchanted with Silk Touch.

implementationNote: Version-gate the spawner loot behavior to Pre4 only; preserve spawner block entity data only if the era evidence supports it. No claim that spawners existed in the project's Infdev profiles.

behaviour: Pre3's enchantment-table prototype could give an item an enchantment glint and the literal tooltip label 'Enchanted!!', despite having no implemented enchantments. Pre4 replaces the placeholder with actual enchantment names/effects, including Feather Falling. Feather Falling is one real enchantment option in Pre4, not a universal enchantment applied to every item.

evidence.quote: Not fully implemented, as no enchantments exist yet.
Enchanted items display "Enchanted!!" on their tooltip, and their name becomes blue.
Enchanted items' tooltips now display their enchantments instead of "Enchanted!!".
Feather Falling

implementationNote: For Pre3 only, an enchanting-result/tooltip hook could render the placeholder label and glint without granting actual enchantment effects. From Pre4, keep actual enchantments and names; do not force Feather Falling onto all results. This profile-specific enchanting behavior is not found in the current gameplay implementation.
